outcome.technical: FINDINGS. P148-R16 (fixed): tests/test_stamp_verification.py replaces the fixed _DEADLINE_LADDER with _ladder(attempt) + _next_rung(deadline, partial_after): each rung is at least double the last, and when a try reached its partial witness (`first`) it is at least 3*(first - try start) + hold + 1; the only top is M.MAX_TIMEOUT, the longest --timeout the helper accepts (a runner that cannot reach the second run inside it cannot make the proof under the helper at all). The final assertion that a rung reached the second run is kept. New pure case sr39a models runners needing up to the ceiling (and one beyond it, which ends at the ceiling). P148-R17 (fixed): _one_deadline_holds uses the `second` stamp as the last sign of life when `beat` is None; new case sr39b checks the fallback passes, and that a stamp or beat past the bound still fails. P148-R25 (fixed, class-wide): every clock bound in the suite was read and each is now derived or shown monotone - sr22 (was --timeout 3 + sleep(6) against a grandchild's sleep(5): both the reach and the absence were speed-bound) now climbs the same ladder, the grandchild stamps start and beats until killed, and after the helper returns its beat file is watched for _QUIET_GAPS times its own longest gap (floor _QUIET_FLOOR); growth = survivor, which is then killed by pid. sr42 (was `spent < 4 + 3*GRACE + 2*REMOVE_GIT_TIMEOUT`) now uses a witness: behind a build slowed by _BUILD_DELAY the run's last beat must be before its own start + deadline - delay/2, on a ladder. sr23/23b/23c: START_DEADLINE 180 -> M.HOST_BASH_LIMIT, polling also stops when the nested helper exits, communicate(timeout=120) -> HOST_BASH_LIMIT, the held command holds until killed instead of sleep(60). sr105/sr111/sr115 (deadline now+5/+30 needing completion, asserting t<=6/31) -> _frozen_git_timeouts: M._left frozen at a whole second, deadline = that + M.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, each git timeout must EQUAL it. sr209, sr187, sd8, sw2, sw10, sw11 (+30/+60) -> _AMPLE_DEADLINE (= M.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). sr139 subprocess timeout=60 and nu2 timeout=120 -> _harness.stage_timeout(). sr215/217/218/219 real-clock waits -> fake ticking clocks. swd1 sized deadline (was 60 s for runs that must finish) -> _SLOW_COST derived so the sized deadline is the helper's default. Left as monotone, each with its reason in the new _CLOCK_LITERALS_JUDGED table: sr9 --timeout 1, sr155 now+0.5, sd9 now-1, swd2's _SHORT_DEFAULT/_SLOW_SECONDS, _FIRST_HOLD, _BEAT. Mechanism: new cases sk1 (AST scan of this file for every literal clock figure - time.time()+/-N, timeout=N, '--timeout' 'N', time.sleep(N), module numeric constants - each must have a row, stale rows red) and sk2 (the scan over a probe: every shape found, a parameter default / string / derived figure not). Not changed, outside the declared files: tests/_harness.py's fixed GIT_TIMEOUT for fixture git and STAGE_TIMEOUT.
